newsitem.title: UK: London BFI rises 31 points on Panamax pressure.
newsitem.headline: London BFI rises 31 points on Panamax pressure.

text.p: Significantly stronger pressure from charterers for Panamax tonnage in nearly all areas except South America propelled the BFI to another dramatic rise, up 31 points today to 1,176.
Three weeks ago the index stood at 1,000 and there was widespread speculation about elderly Panamaxes going into lay-up.
Today the oldest ones afloat are turning to face a transformed Atlantic market. Many brokers believe that Panam rates still have some way to climb, particularly from U.S. Gulf to the Far East.

It is no coincidence that there have been few reports of voyage fixtures in these trades recently. Charterers are resorting more to timecharter, even covering vessels from the steady Pacific market, and "under-the-counter" deals are becoming more frequent.
Handy-size rates have moved up in sympathy in the North Atlantic, but elsewhere the market is quite flat for these types. Capers are still out of favour with limited demand in the mineral trades.
GRAINS --
There is not much prompt Panamax or handy-size tonnage in the North Atlantic and consequently rates are being driven up sharply.

Rumours circulated that Cargill had fixed Polish tonnage and Continental fixed Hyphestos each for about 60,000 heavy grain U.S. Gulf/Holland at a much firmer $12.00 for end Oct/early Nov, but they could not be confirmed.
Glencore was said to have booked 50,000 barley Rostock to Saudi Arabia for end Oct at $18, last fixed having been Continental's fixture on Friday of 80,000 tonnes Antwerp/Dammam at $14.00.

Such is the shortage of early Panamaxes that Ioannis Zafirakis 64,916 dwt is believed fixed delivery prompt Taiwan for a U.S. Gulf round at $9,000 daily and Dorval took Torm Marina 69,637 dwt delivery Gibraltar early Nov for a trip via U.S. Gulf with grain to Taiwan at a strong $12,250 daily.
Athina 68,817 dwt is also rumoured fixed from the Pacific for U.S. Gulf business.
Even a 1972-built 68,000-tonne vessel was said to have been covered from the Continent on subjects for six-eight months at close to $6,000 daily.
In the Far East, North Emperor 67,232 dwt was rumoured taken delivery north China for short period at between $9,750 and $10,000 daily.
Little news emerged about South American grain chartering although Sinochart was linked with Pericles G.C. 65,085 dwt for Plate/China and Minoan Hill 62,593 dwt for Plate/west coast Mexico.

Stronger handy rates were seen with Continental paying $20.00 for 25,000 heavy grain U.S. Gulf/Tunisia and Glencore the same rate for a similar cargo U.S. Gulf/Buenaventura, both for Oct shipment. Cam was linked with a cargo of 30,000 HSS U.S. Gulf/Poland at $16.50.
MINERALS ETC--
A conference in Madrid was said to be reducing activity among coal charterers. Certainly news of Caper business was thin on Monday.
British Steel fixed and failed United Resolve 150,000 dwt delivery Far East for a trip via Australia to UK at $9,500 daily and a CSBC type was rumoured fixed from Taiwan for a trip to the Atlantic.
Leopold L D 165,000 dwt was understood fixed from Port Hedland with iron ore to Immingham and Redcar on private terms.

Panamaxes were reported to be in good demand for coal from South Africa. Samsun were understood to have fixed Global Epica 62,412 dwt Richards Bay/Continent and Pan Ocean booked Ocean Lady 67,688 dwt for similar business.
NSAC fixed and failed with a Panamax Richards Bay/Taiwan and Georgia was rumoured fixed from South Africa on subjects.
Onore shipments were rumoured covered by Noble with Sonata 1 77,987 dwt India/China and by unnamed charterers with Angelic Protector 77,961 dwt Brazil/Continent.
Elsewhere Scanports covered 40,000/10 coke Gdynia/Praia Mole on private terms. Jebsen took an over-age 27,000 dwt vessel from north coast South America to U.S. Gulf at $6,500 daily.
